displays.label: 128x32 RGB332 serial colour display (the "Chroma Corpse" display); CORE_VIDEO layout, handed to LibPinMAME as 16-bit 5.6.5 frames (depth 16)

drivers.variant_notes: Code update V26 (Spooky's rzupdate_V26.zip code update (Google Drive link on spookypinball.com): RZO_V026.PRG, PRP_V008.BIN and the SD card's DMD/ and sound folders), loaded as rzspook_026.zip. Every edition (IPDB 6416 Standard Edition; IPDB 6417 Limited Edition) runs this code on the same board and playfield; PinMAME declares the set as a clone of the unreported pinHeck system set. PinMAME revisions before 97aa922b named it `rzspook`.

physical.notes: Firmware cabinet input 1 (U12 D0), published at 1 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The Switch Edge walk toggled it separately (released, then held again) instead of closing it. The factory chart prints 'Coin Door (closed)' in this cell. pinheck_brd_reset sets it at every reset because the door rests closed; the ROM printed DOOR CLOSE while it was 1 and dropped the text when the host released it, so 1 means the door is closed. Cabinet header pin 'door', wire gray/white.

Firmware cabinet input 2 (U12 D1), published at 2 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure as firmware cabinet 2. PinMAME's port names the bit User; the factory chart leaves it blank and the cabinet header prints 'user0' without a wire colour.

Firmware cabinet input 3 (U12 D2), published at 3 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The Switch Edge walk drives the button through 112 instead, because core_updateSw rewrites this address every vblank. ROM-readable copy of the right flipper button: FLIP_SWNO(4, 3) makes core_updateSw copy public 112 into this address on every vblank, so a host drives 112; a direct write here is overwritten. Cabinet header pin 'R. flipper', wire gray/black.

Firmware cabinet input 4 (U12 D3), published at 4 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The Switch Edge walk drives the button through 114 instead, because core_updateSw rewrites this address every vblank. ROM-readable copy of the left flipper button: FLIP_SWNO(4, 3) makes core_updateSw copy public 114 into this address on every vblank, so a host drives 114; a direct write here is overwritten. Cabinet header pin 'L. flipper', wire gray/red.

Firmware cabinet input 5 (U12 D4), published at 5 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). Not closed in the Switch Edge walk because it leaves the test; every walk used it to leave the test it ran. The factory switch chart leaves the cell blank but the wire chart's cabinet header wires 'menu' here; PinMAME's port names the bit Back, and the ROM leaves a test on it. Cabinet header pin 'menu', wire gray/blue.

Firmware cabinet input 6 (U12 D5), published at 6 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). Not closed in the Switch Edge walk because it restarts the test; every walk opened the operator menu and started its test with it. Cabinet header pin 'enter', wire gray/green.

Firmware cabinet input 7 (U12 D6), published at 7 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure as firmware cabinet 7. Cabinet header pin 'coin mech', wire gray/purp.

Firmware cabinet input 8 (U12 D7), published at 8 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure as firmware cabinet 8. Cabinet header pin 'tilt', wire gray/yellow. While it was held the ROM printed 'SWITCH TEST TILT ACTIVE AUDIO: OFF'.

Factory switch 0, column 0, row 0. The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure at factory switch 0 (column 0, row 0) of its 8x8 grid. pinHeck reads the matrix uncomplemented: board.c pulls a return line low for every closed contact in the strobed column and the driver has no invSw mask, so public 1 is the closed contact. The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure while the host held public 1, so the contact rests open (normally_closed false), whatever its construction.

mechanisms.behavior: Seven balls rest on 12-18 (Trough 1-7); BALL LOAD (18) feeds one to the shooter lane. In the game-start run (all seven contacts closed, Start pressed) the ROM pulsed 18 every 6 s for 20 s, because no ball ever reached the shooter switch.
mechanisms.label: Seven-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: AUTOPLUNGER (17) kicks the ball resting on the shooter lane switch 11 into play; PinMAME's simulator also offers a manual plunger.
mechanisms.label: Shooter lane and autolauncher

mechanisms.behavior: A ROM-driven flipper on two board coils: the cabinet button reaches the ROM as cabinet input 3 (host public 112), the ROM fires the RFLIP HIGH (20) winding to lift the bat and holds it on the RFLIP LOW (19) winding, and the matrix end-of-stroke contact 24 tells it the stroke is complete. PinMAME publishes no Fliptronic states for this platform: the coil addresses are the flipper.
mechanisms.label: Right flipper

mechanisms.behavior: A ROM-driven flipper on two board coils: the cabinet button reaches the ROM as cabinet input 4 (host public 114), the ROM fires the LFLIP HIGH (14) winding to lift the bat and holds it on the LFLIP LOW (13) winding, and the matrix end-of-stroke contact 25 tells it the stroke is complete. PinMAME publishes no Fliptronic states for this platform: the coil addresses are the flipper.
mechanisms.label: Left flipper

mechanisms.behavior: The upper flipper on UFLIP HIGH (3) and UFLIP LOW (8) with its end-of-stroke contact 41; the ROM fires it from the right button.
mechanisms.label: Upper flipper

mechanisms.behavior: The VUK (4) lifts a ball held on 43; 44 (Secret Passage) feeds it.
mechanisms.label: Vertical up-kicker

mechanisms.behavior: A single drop target (48) guards the right inner orbit (35); the Drop Target coil (7) resets it. With it down, the orbit leads to a rail lock: Right Rail Lower (33) and Upper (34) hold balls behind the BALL STOP post (5, the chart's stop post on the right inner orbit), which drops to release one.
mechanisms.label: Drop target and rail lock

mechanisms.behavior: Servo 0 (57, Spaulding) is the gate to the elevated mini-playfield: GATE OPEN and GATE CLOSE in the Servo test. Opto 95 sees the ball at the gate, 37/38 are the upper playfield's switches and opto 96 sees it leave.
mechanisms.label: Spaulding gate and upper playfield

mechanisms.behavior: The animated robot is servo 1 (58): ROBOT START and ROBOT END in the Servo test.
mechanisms.label: Captain Spaulding robot

mechanisms.behavior: The Living Dead Girl figure with targets 46 (right) and 47 (left), lit by the first LED of the external WS2801 chain: LDG RED on 62, LDG GREEN on 64 and LDG BLUE on 63.
mechanisms.label: Living Dead Girl
